| `update_task` | write | draft | Update ONE task: mark it complete and/or set its due date ('today', '+Nd', YYYY-MM-DD). |

## Tool reference

Per-tool parameters, generated from the registry's input schemas —
regenerate with `python scripts/dump_tool_table.py --write`.

<!-- TOOL_DETAILS_START (generated by scripts/dump_tool_table.py) -->
### mail-read

#### `list_folders` — read (min tier: read)

List mail folders as a depth-limited tree walk, or search the entire folder tree when `query` is given. Each row is {id, name, path, total, unread, children}; `id` is a short folder alias (f7) reusable as a `folder`/`parent` argument anywhere. Well-known folders also carry `wk` (e.g. 'f:inbox') — prefer passing that stable alias. Rows also carry the raw EWS FolderClass as `folder_class` when Exchange reports one (e.g. 'IPF.Note' for mail, 'IPF.Appointment' for calendar). Set include_empty=false to hide folders with zero items.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parent` | string | no | Start folder: well-known alias (f:inbox), folder alias (f7), path, or raw id. Default: the message-folder root. |
| `depth` | integer | no | (default `2`) |
| `include_empty` | boolean | no | (default `True`) |
| `query` | string | no | Non-empty case-insensitive substring match on folder name or full path across the whole tree (`depth` is ignored when `query` is set). |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `search_messages` — read (min tier: read)

Search mail. TWO ENGINES, mutually exclusive: pass `query` (an Exchange AQS string, e.g. 'from:alice@example.com subject:rfp hasattachment:yes') OR the structured filters (sender/subject/since/until/is_unread/has_attachments/categories/importance/flag_complete) — combining `query` with any structured filter is a validation error. `sender` is matched client-side against the fetched page's sender email/name, so total_available is unknown when it is used. Results are compact cards, newest first; their `id` values are short aliases (m12) for get_message / get_messages / get_thread / get_attachment. If an id later goes stale (items move), re-run this search for fresh ids.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | no | AQS query string — cannot be combined with the structured filters below. |
| `folder` | string | no | Folder alias (f:inbox, f:sent, f7), path, raw id, or f:all for the whole mailbox: all mail folders with their subfolders, without deleted items, junk, drafts and outbox; each hit then names its folder. (default `f:inbox`) |
| `sender` | string | no | Sender email or display-name substring, matched within each page; keep paging while next_offset is set (a page may hold fewer than `limit` items or none, and total_available is null on live searches). |
| `from_` | string | no | DEPRECATED alias of `sender` — do not combine the two. |
| `subject` | string | no | Subject substring. |
| `since` | string | no | Window start: 'today', '+Nd', YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime (server timezone). |
| `until` | string | no | Window end: 'today', '+Nd', YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime (server timezone). |
| `is_unread` | boolean | no |  |
| `has_attachments` | boolean | no |  |
| `categories` | array | no | Match messages carrying all listed Outlook categories; live search uses contains matching whereas the local mirror matches exact category elements. Cannot combine with `query`. |
| `importance` | string | no | Match messages by importance (high, normal, or low) on both the mirror and live lanes. Cannot combine with `query`. (one of: `high`, `normal`, `low`) |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | Search `folder` and all mail folders under it, merged newest first; each card carries `folder` and the result reports `folders_searched`. Always runs live. (default `False`) |
| `flag_complete` | boolean | no | true matches messages whose follow-up flag is marked Complete; false matches all other messages (unflagged or still-open flag). Always runs live and cannot combine with `query`. |
| `offset` | integer | no | (default `0`) |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default `20`) |
| `mode` | string | no | semantic = hybrid FTS + vector retrieval (only when the semantic tier is enabled; requires `query`; other filters ignored). (one of: `keyword`, `semantic`; default `keyword`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `check_messages` — read (min tier: read)

Check a whole list of values against one mail folder in one call: which values occur as a whole word in a message subject (or in the sender name/address) and which are missing. Returns up to 5 matching cards per value. Use this instead of one search_messages call per value.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `values` | string/array | yes | Values separated by commas or new lines, or an array of strings (a JSON array string is accepted too). At most 200. |
| `field` | string | no | Where to look for each value (default subject). (one of: `subject`, `sender`) |
| `folder` | string | no | Single mail folder alias, path, or raw id, e.g. f:inbox (default) or f:sent (f:all and recursive scopes are not supported). |
| `since` | string | no | Received at or after (ISO date). |
| `until` | string | no | Received at or before (ISO date). |
| `only_missing` | boolean | no | Return only the values without a match. |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `get_message` — read (min tier: read)

Fetch one message by id (short alias from search results, e.g. m12; raw EWS ids also work). format='full' (default) returns recipients, the cleaned body (quoted history stripped — use get_thread for the conversation) and the attachment inventory; format='concise' returns the compact card; format='eml' writes the message MIME content exclusively under DATA_DIR/attachments (adding -2, -3, … rather than overwriting, and refusing above EWS_MAX_ATTACHMENT_MB) and returns only saved_path and size_bytes — a message exported from Sent Items may contain its Bcc header because the file is the message as the mailbox holds it. `flag_complete` is only reported when read live, i.e. with fresh=true. A not_found means the id went stale (items move) — re-run search_messages and retry with a fresh id.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Message id (m-alias or raw). |
| `format` | string | no | (one of: `full`, `concise`, `eml`; default `full`) |
| `include_html` | boolean | no | Also return the raw HTML body (rendering edge cases only — it is token-expensive). (default `False`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `get_messages` — read (min tier: read)

Fetch up to 20 messages by id in one call, preserving the requested order. Returns the canonical envelope {items, count, total_available, next_offset} plus `failed` ({id, index, code, error}) for per-message failures without aborting the remaining ids; when some items come from the local mirror and some live, top-level `source` is 'mixed' and each item carries its own `source` (plus `as_of` on mirror items). format='full' (default) returns the same cleaned message shape as get_message without downloading attachment bytes: PKCS#7 S/MIME attachments are reported as smime_type='candidate' from name and MIME type only, whereas get_message gives the confirmed 'signed'/'enveloped' classification for one message. format='concise' returns compact cards.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array | yes | Message ids (m-aliases or raw EWS ids), 1 to 20 per call. |
| `format` | string | no | (one of: `concise`, `full`; default `full`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `get_thread` — read (min tier: read)

Rebuild the conversation containing the given message id: Inbox and Sent are merged and sorted chronologically, each entry's body cleaned to its latest-reply-only text. Returns thread_id (t-alias), participants with message counts, and the most recent `limit` entries. Entry ids are m-aliases usable with get_message/get_attachment. Stale id → re-run search_messages.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Any message id in the thread (m-alias or raw). |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default `20`) |
| `offset` | integer | no | History paging: 0 = the most recent entries; pass the returned next_offset for older ones. (default `0`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

#### `get_attachment` — read (min tier: read)

Read one attachment of a message. mode='info' → metadata only; 'text' → extracted text in memory (up to 20000 chars from `offset`, with `total_chars`, `next_offset` when more follows, `extracted_from`, and `pages`/`slides`/`sheets` count) for PDF (.pdf, requires ews-mcp[extract]), Word (.docx/.docm), Excel (.xlsx/.xlsm), PowerPoint (.pptx/.pptm), RFC-822 (.eml), attached Exchange messages, HTML (.html/.htm), and plain text (.txt/.csv/.md/.log/.json or text/*; .msg is not supported); 'save' → write the bytes exclusively under DATA_DIR/attachments (adding -2, -3, … rather than overwriting) and return saved_path; 'auto' (default) → text for every supported document/text type, otherwise info plus a hint. An smime.p7m attachment (application/pkcs7-mime) is sniffed and reported as `smime_type: signed|enveloped` — signed is NOT encrypted (auto decodes as text, cert/signature bytes show as replacement chars); enveloped IS encrypted (auto stays info; content is unrecoverable without the recipient's private key). When the message has several attachments you MUST pick one via `attachment` (a name, or a zero-based index as a string).

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message_id` | string | yes | Message id (m-alias or raw). |
| `attachment` | string | no | Attachment name or zero-based index as a string (e.g. '0'). Optional only when the message has exactly one attachment. |
| `mode` | string | no | (one of: `auto`, `info`, `text`, `save`; default `auto`) |
| `offset` | integer | no | Character offset for reading extracted text in parts (pass the returned next_offset for the next chunk). (default `0`) |

#### `get_mailbox_overview` — read (min tier: read)

The morning-brief workflow tool — start here. One call returns unread_total, the 10 most recent unread message cards, today's calendar events (recurrences expanded) across `horizon_days` days, and the Exchange connection state. Card ids are short aliases (m12 / e3) for the other tools.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `horizon_days` | integer | no | (default `1`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read instead of the local mirror (responses are stamped source=cache\|live). (default `False`) |

### calendar / people / status

#### `list_events` — read (min tier: read)

List calendar events overlapping a time window (default: today through +7d, server timezone). Recurring meetings are expanded into individual occurrences — a weekly meeting shows once per occurrence in the window. Returns a paged envelope of compact event cards; their ids are short aliases (e1, e2, …) you pass to get_event.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | string | no | Window start: 'today', '+Nd' (relative days), YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime. (default `today`) |
| `end` | string | no | Window end (exclusive): 'today', '+Nd' (relative days), YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime. (default `+7d`) |
| `offset` | integer | no | Pagination offset into the window. (default `0`) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Max events returned. (default `25`) |

#### `get_event` — read (min tier: read)

Fetch one calendar event in full by id (a short alias like 'e3' from list_events, or a raw EWS id). Returns organizer, every attendee with their response (Accept/Decline/Tentative/…), the cleaned body text, a recurring flag, the rule of a series, the reminder (null if none), your own response and, for an event you organize, whether invitations were sent.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Event id — alias (e1, e2, …) or raw EWS id. |

#### `check_availability` — read (min tier: read)

Check free/busy for one or more attendees and propose meeting slots. Each returned slot is a candidate start/end (30-minute grid) of duration_minutes where EVERY listed attendee is free; per_attendee shows the raw busy blocks behind the answer. With working_hours_only (default true) slots are confined to 09:00-17:00 in the server timezone. An empty slots list means no common free window exists in the range.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attendees` | array | yes | SMTP email addresses to check. |
| `start` | string | yes | Window start: 'today', '+Nd' (relative days), YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime. |
| `end` | string | yes | Window end: 'today', '+Nd' (relative days), YYYY-MM-DD, or ISO datetime. |
| `duration_minutes` | integer | no | Desired meeting length. (default `30`) |
| `working_hours_only` | boolean | no | Confine slots to 09:00-17:00. (default `True`) |

#### `find_people` — read (min tier: read)

Find people by name or email fragment in the GAL (global address list) and/or the personal contacts folder. source='auto' merges both, deduplicating by email with the GAL entry winning. Returned ids are short aliases (p1, p2, …).

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | Name or email fragment, e.g. 'alice@example.com'. |
| `source` | string | no | Where to search; auto = GAL + contacts. (one of: `auto`, `gal`, `contacts`; default `auto`) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Max people returned. (default `10`) |

#### `get_contact` — read (min tier: read)

Fetch one person in full by id — a p-alias from find_people, a raw contact id, or a plain email address. Returns name/email/title/department/office/company/phone where known, plus mirror-derived history (first/last contact, sent/received counts) when the local mirror is warm.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | p-alias, raw contact id, or email. |

#### `get_oof_settings` — read (min tier: read)

Read the mailbox out-of-office (automatic reply) settings: state (disabled/enabled/scheduled), the scheduled window when applicable, and the internal/external reply texts (HTML stripped, capped at 500 chars).

_No parameters._

#### `get_server_status` — read (min tier: read)

This server's own status: version, uptime, Exchange connection state, capability tier, send kill-switch, tool count, per-tool call counters and alias statistics. Never touches Exchange — it answers even while the connection is still warming up, so use it to explain connectivity problems.

_No parameters._

### tasks / waiting-on

#### `list_tasks` — read (min tier: read)

List Exchange tasks (to-dos), incomplete ones by default. Returns {id, subject, due, complete, status}; ids are short aliases (k1, k2, …) for update_task. Served from the local mirror when synced (source=cache), live otherwise.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_completed` | boolean | no | (default `False`) |
| `offset` | integer | no | (default `0`) |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default `25`) |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | true forces a live Exchange read. (default `False`) |

#### `update_task` — write (min tier: draft)

Update ONE task: mark it complete and/or set its due date ('today', '+Nd', YYYY-MM-DD). Nothing else is editable here — task planning belongs to the calling assistant, not the server.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Task id (k-alias from list_tasks or raw). |
| `complete` | boolean | no |  |
| `due` | string | no | New due date: 'today', '+Nd', or YYYY-MM-DD. |

#### `waiting_on` — read (min tier: read)

Deterministic mirror query: messages YOU sent whose thread has received no inbound reply after `days` days — the 'what am I waiting on?' list. Each row carries the sent message id, the thread alias, recipients and a snippet. Requires the local mirror (sent folder synced).

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `days` | integer | no | (default `5`) |
| `limit` | integer | no | (default `25`) |

### writes

#### `create_draft` — write (min tier: draft)

Author mail as a DRAFT (never sends). mode=new needs to+body; reply/reply_all/forward need reply_to (the original message id) and quote the original server-side; forward also needs to. body_format='text' (default) escapes plain text; 'html' rebuilds markup through an allow-list sanitiser and reports removals in sanitised. importance applies to mode=new only. attachments adds files; if one fails the draft still exists and attachments_failed names it. Use send_draft to send.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | no | (one of: `new`, `reply`, `reply_all`, `forward`; default `new`) |
| `reply_to` | string | no |  |
| `to` | array | no |  |
| `cc` | array | no |  |
| `bcc` | array | no |  |
| `subject` | string | no |  |
| `body` | string | yes |  |
| `body_format` | string | no | text (default, escaped and wrapped in minimal HTML) or html (rebuilt through an allow-list sanitiser; remote images, scripts, forms and non-http/https/mailto links are stripped). (one of: `text`, `html`; default `text`) |
| `importance` | string | no | (one of: `normal`, `high`) |
| `attachments` | array | no |  |

#### `update_draft` — write (min tier: draft)

Update fields of an existing draft (to/cc/bcc/subject/body) and/or remove attachments by name or id (remove_attachments). Only the supplied fields change; body uses body_format ('text' by default, or sanitised 'html'). remove_attachments matches all selectors before any write (all-or-nothing matching), refuses ambiguous names with the attachment ids to choose from, detaches before saving other fields, and returns remaining attachments (or removed + remaining attachments if a multi-delete fails mid-way).

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | yes |  |
| `to` | array | no |  |
| `cc` | array | no |  |
| `bcc` | array | no |  |
| `subject` | string | no |  |
| `body` | string | no |  |
| `body_format` | string | no | text (default, escaped and wrapped in minimal HTML) or html (rebuilt through an allow-list sanitiser; remote images, scripts, forms and non-http/https/mailto links are stripped). (one of: `text`, `html`; default `text`) |
| `remove_attachments` | array | no | Attachment names or attachment ids (a-aliases or raw ids) to remove from the draft (all-or-nothing selector matching before any deletion). |

#### `add_draft_attachment` — write (min tier: draft)

Add one attachment to an existing draft via content_base64, a relative path inside EWS_ATTACHMENT_DIR, or message_id (attaches a mail message's MIME content with Bcc/Resent-Bcc stripped as a message/rfc822 .eml file named after its sanitised subject, checking declared size before download and refusing non-mail items or the draft itself; the three forms are mutually exclusive). Refuses items that are not in f:drafts. Returns the added attachment and all attachments on the draft (with short a-alias ids).

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | yes |  |
| `filename` | string | no | File name; required with content_base64, defaults to the file's own name when path is given, or to the sanitised subject (.eml) when message_id is given. |
| `content_base64` | string | no | The file content, base64-encoded (mutually exclusive with path and message_id). |
| `path` | string | no | Relative file path inside EWS_ATTACHMENT_DIR (mutually exclusive with content_base64 and message_id). |
| `message_id` | string | no | Existing mail message id (m-alias or raw id; not the draft itself or a non-mail item) to attach as a message/rfc822 .eml file built from its MIME content with Bcc/Resent-Bcc stripped (mutually exclusive with content_base64 and path). |
| `content_type` | string | no | MIME type; derived from the file name if omitted (always message/rfc822 when message_id is given). |

#### `delete_draft` — write (min tier: draft)

Move a draft to trash (recoverable). Refuses items that are not in f:drafts.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | yes |  |

#### `update_messages` — write (min tier: draft)

Bulk-update up to 50 messages: set_read, categories_add/categories_remove, and/or flag_complete. Per-item failures are isolated and reported. flag_complete marks/unmarks the message's follow-up flag as Complete (true) or clears completion (false) - it does not raise a NEW follow-up flag on an unflagged message, only sets/clears the completion state.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array | yes |  |
| `set_read` | boolean | no |  |
| `categories_add` | array | no |  |
| `categories_remove` | array | no |  |
| `flag_complete` | boolean | no |  |

#### `move_messages` — write (min tier: draft)

Move up to 50 messages to a folder (id, f:alias or path). Message ids are re-bound automatically: the SAME id keeps working after the move.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array | yes |  |
| `to_folder` | string | yes |  |

#### `create_event` — write (min tier: draft)

Create a calendar event or, with recurrence, a recurring series. Default send_invitations=false saves it like a draft WITHOUT emailing attendees (no confirm needed): they stay on the event, and the organizer can send it from Outlook. With send_invitations=true, invitations leave the org: two-phase confirm + send kill-switch apply. Without reminder_minutes the event has no reminder.

> Two-phase confirm for some argument combinations: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subject` | string | yes |  |
| `start` | string | yes |  |
| `end` | string | yes |  |
| `attendees` | array | no |  |
| `location` | string | no |  |
| `body` | string | no |  |
| `reminder_minutes` | integer | no | Remind this many minutes before the start; 0 is at the start. |
| `recurrence` | object | no | Repeat the event. start and end are the first occurrence; the time of day stays the same across DST changes. Without until or count the series has no end. |
| `send_invitations` | boolean | no | (default `False`) |

#### `update_event` — write (min tier: draft)

Update event fields (subject/start/end/location/body/reminder). An occurrence id from list_events changes that occurrence only; scope='series' changes the whole series and overwrites those fields on occurrences changed individually before. Default notify_attendees=false is a silent metadata edit; true notifies changed attendees → two-phase confirm + send kill-switch apply.

> Two-phase confirm for some argument combinations: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string | yes |  |
| `subject` | string | no |  |
| `start` | string | no |  |
| `end` | string | no |  |
| `location` | string | no |  |
| `body` | string | no |  |
| `reminder_minutes` | integer | no | Remind this many minutes before the start; 0 is at the start, -1 removes the reminder. |
| `scope` | string | no | For recurring events. With 'series', start and end must be on the series' first date. (one of: `occurrence`, `series`) |
| `notify_attendees` | boolean | no | (default `False`) |

#### `send_draft` — send (min tier: full)

Send an existing draft (the ONLY way mail leaves this mailbox). Two-phase: the first call fetches the draft and returns its REAL recipients/subject/body/attachments/links (with warnings on mismatched link text) as a preview + confirm_token bound to that content (attachments bound by name, size, and id, not a content hash); the second call with the token re-verifies the content and sends (editing the draft in between invalidates the token). Optional idempotency_key dedupes retries (replays return the stored result).

> Two-phase confirm for some argument combinations: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `draft_id` | string | yes |  |
| `idempotency_key` | string | no |  |

#### `respond_to_event` — send (min tier: full)

Accept/tentative/decline a meeting — this SENDS a response to the organizer, so it is two-phase confirmed.

> Two-phase confirm: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string | yes |  |
| `response` | string | yes | (one of: `accept`, `decline`, `tentative`) |
| `message` | string | no |  |

#### `cancel_event` — destructive (min tier: full)

Cancel a meeting you organize (sends cancellations to attendees, checked by the recipient guard and external-recipient warning) or move a plain non-meeting appointment without attendees to Deleted Items (nothing sent). Fails closed on non-calendar items and meetings organized by someone else or with an unverified organizer — use respond_to_event instead. Destructive, two-phase confirmed; the preview states action ('cancel' or 'delete'), attendee_count, start, end, and whole-series status, and binds them into the token.

> Two-phase confirm: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_id` | string | yes |  |
| `message` | string | no |  |

#### `delete_messages` — destructive (min tier: full)

Delete up to 50 messages. disposition: 'trash' (default, recoverable), 'soft' (dumpster) or 'permanent' (UNRECOVERABLE — requires two-phase confirm). Class is destructive, so ALL dispositions need the full tier in v5.0 (conservative).

> Two-phase confirm for some argument combinations: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | array | yes |  |
| `disposition` | string | no | (one of: `trash`, `soft`, `permanent`; default `trash`) |

#### `set_oof` — send (min tier: full)

Set out-of-office auto-replies (externally visible → send class, two-phase confirmed). state: disabled|enabled|scheduled; scheduled needs start+end. external_reply defaults to internal_reply when omitted.

> Two-phase confirm: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | string | yes | (one of: `disabled`, `enabled`, `scheduled`) |
| `internal_reply` | string | no |  |
| `external_reply` | string | no |  |
| `start` | string | no |  |
| `end` | string | no |  |

### inbox rules

#### `list_rules` — read (min tier: read)

List server-side Exchange Inbox rules. Reports every rule with an r-alias id, conditions, actions, and editable=true|false (plus unsupported fields, sends_mail/recipients for rules that send or forward mail, and in_error when Exchange flagged the rule). Top-level outlook_only_rules (true|false|null) indicates whether Outlook-only client rules exist that any EWS rule write would remove.

_No parameters._

#### `save_rule` — write (min tier: draft)

Create a server-side Inbox rule or wholesale-replace an existing editable rule (pass rule_id to replace). Only mailbox-internal actions are allowed (move_to_folder, copy_to_folder, assign_categories, mark_as_read, mark_importance, stop_processing_rules); sending/forwarding/deleting actions and Deleted Items/Junk targets are refused, and rules with editable=false cannot be replaced. Always two-phase confirmed; warns when conditions are empty or Outlook-only rules would be lost.

> Two-phase confirm: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `actions` | object | yes | Mailbox-internal rule actions (at least one must be enabled). Sending, forwarding, redirecting, server replies, and deleting are never writable. |
| `conditions` | object | no | Predicates an incoming message must match. Omitting conditions or passing {} matches every incoming message (warned in preview). |
| `priority` | integer | no | Execution order (1 runs first; defaults to 1 on create, or keeps the current priority on replace). |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Whether the rule is active (defaults to true on create, or keeps the current state on replace). |
| `rule_id` | string | no | Existing r-alias to wholesale-replace; omit to create. |

#### `delete_rule` — write (min tier: draft)

Delete a server-side Inbox rule by rule_id (including rules reported with editable=false). Always two-phase confirmed; warns when Outlook-only rules exist on the mailbox.

> Two-phase confirm: the first call returns a preview + `confirm_token`; repeat the call with the token to execute.

| parameter | type | required | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rule_id` | string | yes |  |

Find messages semantically similar to a given one (vector similarity over cleaned bodies; Arabic + English). Returns compact cards with a `similarity` score. Only available when the optional semantic tier is enabled.

## The canonical envelope

Every list-shaped tool ships exactly:

```json
{"ok": true, "items": [...], "count": 3, "total_available": 120,
 "next_offset": 3, "source": "cache", "as_of": "2026-07-11T04:00:00+00:00"}
```

- `count` = `len(items)`; `total_available` is exact when cheap (local
  mirror `COUNT(*)`, a refreshed folder count on unfiltered live
  listings, or live single-folder `categories` / `flag_complete=true`
  queries without `query` or `sender`) and `null` otherwise. In
  particular, `total_available` is `null` on live
  `search_messages(flag_complete=false)` or live `importance`-filtered
  searches without `categories`/`flag_complete=true` (counting matching
  items could walk most of the folder) and on multi-folder
  `search_messages` (`folder="f:all"` or `recursive=true`) whenever any
  folder has matches past `offset + limit`, any folder fails
  (`folders_failed`), folders exceed the 200-folder cap
  (`folders_skipped`), or `sender` is set. `next_offset` is `null` when
  no further page exists (live paths prove it with a one-item lookahead,
  never a `count()` scan). `get_messages` ships the same canonical
  envelope plus `failed` (`[{id, index, code, error}]`, carrying each
  caller-supplied `id` verbatim and its zero-based `index` in `ids`) for
  per-id failures.
- `source` is `cache` (with `as_of`), `live`, or — on `get_messages` when
  some returned items come from the mirror and some live — `mixed` (with
  each item carrying its own `source`, plus `as_of` on mirror rows); pass
  `fresh: true` to any cache-first tool to force a live read.

## Ids

All ids in outputs are short aliases: `m` message, `d` draft, `a` attachment,
`e` event, `t` thread, `p` person, `k` task, `f` folder, `r` rule. Inputs accept
aliases or raw EWS ids. A stale alias returns `not_found` with a re-search hint —
ids change when items move; re-run the search or `list_rules` for fresh ones.

## Error taxonomy

| code | HTTP | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `validation` | 400 | bad arguments (schema-checked on the REST shim) |
| `auth_failed` | 401 | missing/invalid `MCP_API_KEY`, Exchange rejected credentials (HTTP 401), or the lockout guard (`AuthBreaker`) is open (retrying will not help) |
| `tier_blocked` | 403 | tool needs a higher `EWS_CAPABILITY_TIER` |
| `kill_switch` | 403 | send-class call while `SEND_ENABLED=false` |
| `recipient_blocked` | 403 | recipient failed the allow/denylist |
| `not_found` | 404 | stale/unknown id (hint: re-search) |
| `confirm_invalid` | 409 | confirm token expired / consumed / content changed |
| `throttled` | 429 | Exchange back-off (`retry_after_s` included) |
| `rate_capped` | 429 | send rate cap reached (`retry_after_s` included) |
| `internal` | 500 | unexpected internal server error |
| `upstream_error` | 502 | Exchange failed the call |
| `upstream_unavailable` | 503 | connection cold/circuit open (`retry_after_s`) |

## Two-phase confirmation

Irreversible or standing-order tools (`send_draft`, `respond_to_event`,
`cancel_event`, `set_oof`, `save_rule`, `delete_rule`, `delete_messages`
with `disposition=permanent`, event tools when they would notify
attendees) run in two phases:

1. Call WITHOUT `confirm_token` → a preview + a short-lived token.
   Nothing executes. For `send_draft` the preview shows the draft's REAL
   `to`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `body_snippet`, `attachment_count`,
   `attachments`, `link_hosts` (ordered with hosts of mismatching links
   first, then other link hosts, then `embedded: true` non-anchor hosts,
   then `unparsed: true` hosts found only by scanning the raw body text,
   capped at 50 with `link_hosts_total` and setting `links_unverified:
   true` when above 50), `links` (up to 20 distinct `{text, href}` pairs
   with mismatching links listed first and `text` cut to 120 characters,
   plus `links_total` when more exist), `warnings` (ordered by severity so
   critical notices — unverified/size, mismatch warnings, targets outside
   normal markup, and omission notices — come first and are never cut,
   while other warning kinds fold beyond three into one line with a count),
   and `links_unverified: true` whenever the stored HTML could not be
   inspected completely (see "Draft bodies" below for the four promises and
   what is not promised). The token is HMAC-bound to subject, sorted
   recipients, text and HTML body, and attachments (bound by `name`, `size`,
   and `id` — not by a hash of attachment content).
   For `cancel_event`, each phase makes one projected fetch and runs an
   explicit fail-closed decision table: non-`CalendarItem` entries fail with
   `validation`; `my_response_type="Organizer"` cancels when `is_meeting` is
   true or any attendee list is non-empty and deletes when `is_meeting` is
   false and all attendee lists are empty; attendee response types (`Accept`,
   `Decline`, `Tentative`, `NoResponseReceived`) fail with `validation`
   pointing to `respond_to_event`; and `Unknown` or missing response types
   delete only when `is_meeting` is explicitly false and all attendee lists
   are empty, compare the organizer's SMTP address against the account's own
   addresses when `is_meeting` is true (ours → cancel; foreign →
   `validation` pointing to `respond_to_event`; missing or non-SMTP →
   `validation`), and fail with `validation` when `is_meeting` is missing.
   When `action` is `"cancel"`, the resolved `attendees` pass through the
   recipient allow/denylist guard and external-recipient warning just like
   `send_draft`. The preview reports `action` (`"cancel"` or `"delete"`),
   `attendee_count`, `start`, `end`, `type`, and — on a recurring master
   (`type="RecurringMaster"`) — `series: true`, `scope: "series"`, and a
   series warning `note`; the token binds `event_id`, `action`, `subject`,
   `start`, `end`, `type`, `series`, `is_meeting`, sorted `attendees`, and
   `message`. For `save_rule` and
   `delete_rule`, the token binds
   the planned rule (including raw target folder ids), the rule it
   replaces or deletes (including a SHA-256 fingerprint of its serialised
   XML), and the `outlook_only_rules` flag; unrelated rules changing in
   between do not invalidate it.
2. Call again with identical arguments plus `confirm_token` → executes
   once. For `send_draft`, phase 2 fetches the draft once under the
   per-draft lock, re-checks its content hash against the verified hash,
   and sends that same object; a draft (or attachment list — including an
   attachment removed via `update_draft(remove_attachments=…)` or a
   message attached via `add_draft_attachment(message_id=…)`) changed
   after the preview is refused with `confirm_invalid`. For `cancel_event`,
   phase 2 fetches the projected calendar entry once, re-verifies the bound
   hash (including `start`, `end`, and `type`), and either cancels the
   meeting (`cancelled: true`) or moves the plain appointment to Deleted
   Items with `SEND_TO_NONE` (`deleted: true`, never a hard delete). For `save_rule`
   and `delete_rule`, phase 2 runs under the in-process `_rules_lock` and
   re-verifies the bound rule state before mutating Exchange. Tokens also
   die on argument changes, on TTL expiry (`CONFIRM_TTL_SECONDS`, default
   600 s), and after one use. `send_draft` retries with the same
   `idempotency_key` replay the cached receipt instead of sending twice.

## Cache freshness contract

Reads served by the local mirror carry `source: "cache"` and `as_of`
(the folder's last sync watermark; delta cadence
`EWS_CACHE_SYNC_SECONDS`, default 45 s). `fresh: true` forces live.
`get_server_status.cache` exposes per-folder watermarks, row counts, DB
size and sync health, including `sync.role` (`"leader"` for the process
holding `cache/sync.lock` and running `SyncEngine`, or `"follower"` for
additional processes reading the shared mirror without running background
sync). `mode: "semantic"` on `search_messages` (and the `find_similar`
tool) exist only when `EWS_SEMANTIC_INDEX` is enabled.

## Searching several folders

`search_messages` supports two live multi-folder modes (`source: "live"`):

- `folder="f:all"` searches every `IPF.Note*` mail folder in the mailbox
  except Deleted Items (`f:trash` / `f:deleteditems`), Junk (`f:junk` /
  `f:junkemail`), Drafts (`f:drafts`), Outbox (`f:outbox`), and their
  subfolders.
- `recursive=true` searches the target `folder` and all `IPF.Note*`
  subfolders beneath it. When `folder` explicitly names Deleted Items,
  Junk, Drafts, or Outbox with `recursive=true`, that subtree is walked.

Each folder in scope is queried for up to `offset + limit` items and
merged newest first (`datetime_received` descending). Multi-folder calls
are bounded to at most `200` folders per call and `offset + limit <= 500`
(exceeding `500` fails with `validation`). If Exchange throttles any
folder, the call fails with `throttled`.

Every returned message card includes `folder` (its folder path), and the
envelope adds `folders_searched`, plus `folders_failed` (paths of
folders that failed, when non-empty) and `folders_skipped` (folders past
the `200`-folder cap, when non-zero). `sender` is matched within each
merged `offset..offset + limit` page, so a page can contain fewer than
`limit` items (or zero) while older matches remain; keep paging while
`next_offset` is non-null.

## Draft attachments

- **Adding files or messages (`add_draft_attachment`, `create_draft`).**
  `add_draft_attachment` accepts exactly one of three mutually exclusive
  sources: `content_base64` (with `filename`), a relative `path` inside
  `EWS_ATTACHMENT_DIR`, or `message_id` (an existing mail message — non-mail
  items and the draft itself are refused with `validation`). With
  `message_id`, the source message's declared `size` is checked against
  `EWS_MAX_ATTACHMENT_MB` before downloading `mime_content` (and the byte
  length is checked again after download), `Bcc` and `Resent-Bcc` headers
  (folded lines included) are removed from the copy before attaching, and
  the `.eml` filename strips format and control characters (bidi marks,
  zero-width characters, C0/C1 controls), prefixes a leading `_` onto
  reserved Windows device stems (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`,
  `LPT1`–`LPT9`), and caps the stem at 120 characters and 200 UTF-8 bytes
  before `.eml` (`message.eml` fallback). Returned attachment entries carry
  short `a`-alias `id` values alongside `name` and `size`. On `send_draft`,
  each attachment is bound into the confirmation token by `name`, `size`,
  and `id` (not by a hash of its byte content).
- **Removing attachments (`update_draft(remove_attachments=[…])`).**
  Each entry in `remove_attachments` is an attachment name or attachment
  id (`a`-alias or raw EWS attachment id). Selector **matching** is
  all-or-nothing under the per-draft lock before any Exchange write runs
  (and refuses items outside `f:drafts`): an unknown entry fails with
  `validation` naming the selector (cut to 80 characters) without modifying
  the draft, and an attachment name matching more than one attachment fails
  with `validation` listing the `a`-alias ids to choose from. Attachment
  removals run **before** saving other draft fields (`to`, `cc`, `bcc`,
  `subject`, `body`): Because Exchange deletes one attachment per server
  call, if a removal fails after earlier removals in the same call
  succeeded, no other draft field has been changed and the error carries
  `removed` and the remaining `attachments` so the caller can continue from
  the real state. On full success, returns the remaining `attachments`.

## Draft bodies

`create_draft` and `update_draft` accept `body_format`: `"text"` (the
default, which HTML-escapes plain text and wraps paragraphs in `<p>`) or
`"html"` (for structured or right-to-left mail). Calendar event bodies
remain plain text only.

- **Allow-list rebuild (`ewsmcp.htmlsafe`).** With `body_format="html"`,
  the input is scanned in one linear-time non-raising pass (custom
  stdlib-only tokenizer, never `html.parser`, executed off the event loop;
  trailing `/` is ignored on non-void HTML elements; numeric character
  references in attribute values decode with or without `;`, while named
  character references in attributes decode only when terminated with `;`
  so query parameters like `&region=sa` stay verbatim; runs of more than 30
  combining marks are cut to 30) and
  serialised anew as `<html><body…>…</body></html>` with every text node
  and attribute value escaped (`dir`, `lang`, `align`, and `style` on
  input `<html>` or `<body>` are carried onto output `<body>`, with
  `<body>` winning; omitted `</head>` closes automatically at `<body>` or
  the first non-head element; implied end tags close `<p>`, `<li>`, and
  table cells/rows/sections the way browsers do; anchors with no visible
  text anywhere in their descendants — table cells included — are removed
  and counted in `removed_links`; and the output is re-sanitised to a fixed
  point while keeping first-pass removal counts). Allowed elements:
  `p`, `br`, `div`, `span`, `b`, `strong`, `i`, `em`, `u`, `s`, `strike`,
  `sub`, `sup`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`,
  `tr`, `td`, `th`, `caption`, `colgroup`, `col`, `h1`–`h6`, `blockquote`,
  `pre`, `code`, `hr`, `a`, `font`. Active, embedded, form, foreign, and
  image elements (`script`, `style`, `head`, `title`, `meta`, `link`,
  `base`, `object`, `embed`, `iframe`, `frame`, `frameset`, `applet`,
  `noembed`, `noframes`, `form`, `input`, `button`, `select`, `option`,
  `textarea`, `svg`, `math`, `template`, `noscript`, `audio`, `video`,
  `source`, `track`, `canvas`, `map`, `area`, `img`) are dropped
  (containers together with their contents, with `script`, `style`,
  `title`, `textarea`, `noembed`, `noframes`, `xmp`, `iframe`, and
  `plaintext` scanned using HTML5 raw-text rules; `img` is excluded so
  remote URLs cannot act as a tracking or exfiltration channel), bidi
  override controls (`U+202D` and `U+202E`) are stripped from text, and
  other unknown tags are unwrapped keeping their text. Comments, marked
  sections, CDATA, processing instructions, and doctypes are stripped.
- **Attributes, links, and `style`.** Global attributes are `dir`
  (`ltr|rtl|auto`), `lang`, `align` (`left|right|center|justify`), and
  `style`; element-specific attributes are `href`/`title` on `a`,
  `colspan`/`rowspan`/`width`/`height` on `td`/`th`,
  `border`/`cellpadding`/`cellspacing`/`width` on `table`,
  `face`/`size`/`color` on `font`, `start`/`type` on `ol`, and
  `span`/`width` on `col` (all `on…` handlers and unknown attributes are
  dropped). `a[href]` permits only `http`, `https`, and single-address
  `mailto` (scheme checked after decoding character references and
  stripping whitespace and control characters; `mailto:` query/fragment
  parts and extra recipients are stripped and counted in `removed_links`,
  and refused or unparseable `href` values are removed while keeping the
  link text). `style` normalises internal whitespace, splits declarations,
  and keeps only safe typography, colour, spacing, border, dimension, and
  list properties (`unicode-bidi` allows only
  `normal|embed|isolate|plaintext`; `font-size` of `0` or below `6px`/`6pt`
  is dropped) whose values are at most 200 characters, free of `url(`,
  `expression`, `@`, `\`, `<`, `>`, `/*`, and `javascript`, and composed
  solely of letters (including non-Latin font names), digits, spaces, and
  `# % . , ( ) ' " - + !`.
- **Refusals and reporting.** The 200,000-character limit applies to the
  input string (escaped output may be longer); inputs above 200,000
  characters or leaving no visible non-blank text after sanitising (blank
  fillers such as `U+3164` and `U+2800` do not count as visible) fail with
  `validation` before saving. `create_draft` (and `update_draft` when
  `body` is supplied) returns `body_format` and, only when markup or link
  parts were stripped, `sanitised: {removed_elements, removed_attributes,
  removed_links}`. On `send_draft`, phase 1 inspects URL-bearing attributes
  (`href`, `xlink:href`, `action`, `formaction`, `src`, `srcset`,
  `background`, `poster`, `data`, `cite`) via the tokenizer (up to
  2,000,000 characters) and also takes the **union over six readings of the
  raw body text** (`http`, `https`, `ftp`, `ftps`, `ws`, `wss`, `file`,
  scheme-relative `//`, and `mailto:`, without quote or markup parsing):
  three character-reference readings (**none** decoded; **as a browser
  decodes** — numeric always with or without `;`, named with `;`, and the
  legacy HTML5 names without `;` only; and **everything decoded to a fixed
  point of three passes**) crossed with two whitespace readings (tab, CR,
  and LF **deleted**, and tab, CR, and LF **replaced by a space**):

  | preview field | meaning |
  |---|---|
  | `link_hosts` | Up to 50 `{host, count[, as_written][, embedded][, unparsed]}` entries ordered with hosts of mismatching links first, then other link hosts, then `embedded: true` non-anchor hosts, then `unparsed: true` hosts found only by the raw-text union scan (`as_written` on IDN/punycode or trailing-dot hosts; hosts over 253 characters are cut to 80 characters with a warning and not passed to IDNA), plus `link_hosts_total` and `links_unverified: true` when more than 50 exist. |
  | `links` | Up to 20 distinct `{text, href}` pairs from parsed `<a>` elements with mismatching links listed first (`text` cut to 120 characters; `unparsed` raw-scan hosts never add to `links`), plus `links_total` when more exist. |
  | `warnings` | Ordered before the 20-item cap as: unverified and size notices; then the singular hosts-omitted notice and outside-normal-markup notice (each exists at most once); then mismatch warnings (including `mailto:` links with multiple recipients or query parameters), shown up to 100 with one count line beyond 100 saying how many more mismatching links exist and setting `links_unverified: true`; then everything else (numeric addresses, overlong hosts, IDN/punycode, malformed/non-anchor URLs, empty links — each folded into one count line beyond three). Critical notices are never cut; `warnings_total` is included whenever warnings were folded or capped. |
  | `links_unverified` | `true` when the stored body exceeds 2,000,000 characters (hosts come from the raw-text union scan only), when `link_hosts` exceeds 50, when mismatch warnings exceed 100, or on an internal inspection error. |

- **What draft HTML and `send_draft` preview promise (and what they do not).**
  Four promises are kept:
  1. **Sanitised bodies are exact**: for any body written through
     `sanitise_html`, its links, their text, and mismatch warnings are
     accurate because this server wrote the markup.
  2. **Every URL host in the text is surfaced**: for any stored body,
     `link_hosts` includes the union over six readings of the raw text
     (character references: none decoded, browser rules, and 3-pass fixed
     point; whitespace: tab/CR/LF deleted and replaced by a space; marked
     `unparsed: true` when outside parsed links), or `links_unverified` is
     `true`.
  3. **Critical notices are never cut**: unverified and size notices come
     first, then the singular "hosts omitted" and "outside normal markup"
     notices, then mismatch warnings (up to 100, followed by a count line
     and `links_unverified: true` when more exist), ahead of all folded
     non-critical warnings.
  4. **Bounded cost and GIL time**: `sanitise_html` runs in under 2 s up to
     200,000 characters; `inspect_draft_links` runs in under 5 s up to
     2,000,000 characters (above which it runs the raw-text host scan only
     and sets `links_unverified: true`), and neither holds the Python
     interpreter lock for more than ~0.2 s in a single library call.

  Two things are **not** promised:
  - Pairing link text with link target inside quoted or otherwise foreign
    HTML that this server did not write.
  - Detecting look-alike characters in link text beyond one rule: removing
    whitespace of any kind around dots before matching host-like tokens,
    and warning when a whitespace-free link-text token mixes ASCII letters
    with any non-ASCII character (pure non-Latin link text such as Arabic
    gets no warning).
## Reading attachments

`get_attachment` extracts readable text strictly in memory — document formats
run inside a per-document isolated child process (`python -m ewsmcp.extract_child`),
while plain-text attachments decode and slice directly in the server process
without spawning a worker — and no attachment is executed, opened in an external
helper program, or written to disk unless the caller explicitly requests
`mode="save"` (which writes exclusively under `DATA_DIR/attachments`, adding `-2`,
`-3`, … when a name already exists, capping the stem at 200 UTF-8 bytes, and
reporting `internal` without tripping the Exchange circuit breaker if the folder
cannot be written):

- **Worker isolation, limits, and security boundary.** Attachment bytes (or
  attached-message fields) are fetched on the Exchange gateway and the gateway
  thread is released before parsing starts. Document formats (`pdf`, `docx`,
  `xlsx`, `pptx`, `eml`, `message`, `html`) run in `ewsmcp.extract_child` (at
  most `2` concurrent workers via an `asyncio` semaphore; cancelling a call
  kills its child immediately and holds the concurrency slot until the
  supervisor finishes), which loads only the Python standard library,
  `defusedxml`, and `ewsmcp` extraction modules (`pypdf` is imported only when a
  PDF arrives; `exchangelib`, `mcp`, `requests`, and server/gateway/tool modules
  are never loaded). Each child runs with a scrubbed environment (no `USERNAME`,
  `EWS_*`, `MCP_*`, `SEND_*`, or `*PASSWORD*` / `*SECRET*` / `*TOKEN*` / `*KEY*`
  variables), `PATH` reduced to the Python interpreter's directory (plus Windows
  `System32` / base prefix when required to start a process), standard error
  discarded (`DEVNULL`), a fresh empty temporary working directory removed with
  retry after the child exits, a `20`-second wall-clock deadline (Win32
  kill-on-close Job Object on Windows; dedicated session via
  `start_new_session=True` + process-group `SIGKILL` on POSIX so no child or
  grandchild process can outlive the call), a self-applied `1,024` MB memory
  ceiling set by the child on its own interpreter process before reading `stdin`
  (Win32 Job Object on Windows, `RLIMIT_AS` on Linux; on other platforms the
  child continues and `get_server_status.document_memory_ceiling` reports
  `enforced: false` with a note), and strict parent-side hostile-input
  validation of the child's JSON response (allow-listed fields, fixed
  `extracted_from` values, bounded integer counts, at most `50` raw notes of at
  most `300` characters, `text` capped at `5,000,000` characters, and lone
  surrogates replaced with `U+FFFD` in every string; nothing the child reports
  about itself is used for a server decision). Long honest documents check
  elapsed time between units of work (PDF pages, Excel sheets, PowerPoint
  slides, Word blocks, MIME message parts) and stop cleanly once `75%` of the
  deadline is used, returning `partial: true`, the unit count read (`pages_read`,
  `slides_read`, `sheets_read`), and `notes` naming where extraction stopped. A
  worker whose first unit hangs past the hard deadline, exceeds memory, cannot
  apply its ceiling on Windows/Linux, exits non-zero, or emits malformed JSON
  fails closed with `validation` (`"the document could not be read within the
  time and memory limits"`). If the server's own temporary directory or worker
  process cannot be created, `get_attachment` reports `internal` (`"Document
  reader is unavailable..."`) without counting toward or opening the Exchange
  circuit breaker.
  - **What the worker protects against, and what it does not:** the worker
    contains **time, memory, and parser crashes** so a pathological or malformed
    file cannot stall or crash the MCP server process. It is **not** an OS user
    or filesystem sandbox: code executing inside a compromised parser runs under
    the server's OS user account and could read or write files accessible to
    that account. On Linux, the server marks itself non-dumpable
    (`prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)`) before starting its first child so processes
    running as the same OS user cannot read `/proc/<pid>/environ` or server
    memory; set `EWS_KEEP_DUMPABLE=true` only when debugging requires core dumps
    or `ptrace` on the server process.
- **Supported types (`mode="auto"` and `mode="text"`).**
  - **PDF (`.pdf`, `extracted_from: "pdf"`, `pages`, `pages_read`)** via the
    optional extra `ews-mcp[extract]` (`pypdf>=6.21,<7`, pre-installed in the
    Docker image). Extracts up to `500` pages in `layout` mode via
    `ewsmcp.pdftext`. On each page, plain-mode text (from an unpatched reader
    when ligature maps were rewritten) is also taken when the layout text is
    empty, when the page's `/Resources` hold a Form `/XObject` (`/Subtype
    /Form`), or when the page has right-to-left letters; when layout text is
    empty and plain text is non-empty, or when plain text has at least `20` more
    non-space characters than layout text and more than `1.2×` as many (for
    example rotated text matrices, rotating `cm`, skewed OCR layers, or Form
    XObjects invisible to `layout` mode), the page's plain-mode text is used
    with a note that the page was read in file order. Pages with no
    right-to-left letters and no invisible Form XObject text are returned
    byte-identical to `layout` mode without a second pass. On pages with
    right-to-left letters, multi-letter right-to-left `/ToUnicode` ligatures in
    `bfchar` and `bfrange` (expanding single start-string ranges of up to `256`
    codes into reversed arrays and leaving larger ranges untouched) are
    rewritten to visual order in memory on the layout reader, lines up to
    `5,000` characters (after collapsing spaces) are converted to reading order
    using either Microsoft Word's layout rules (when Producer/Creator names
    whole-word `Word`) or Unicode rules, Arabic presentation forms and shared
    Persian letter variants (`U+06CC`, `U+06BE`, `U+06A9` when no
    Persian/Urdu-only letters appear on the page) are mapped to searchable
    Arabic base letters, and words split by stray layout spaces are repaired
    linearly against the page's plain-mode text (joining at most `12` pieces).
    Lines longer than `5,000` characters after collapsing spaces are returned
    unconverted with a note. `"PDF has no text layer"` is reported only when
    both `layout` and `plain` passes are empty across all pages.
    - **What is promised, and what is not (PDF reading order):**
      - Arabic words and sentences come out in reading order; Latin words and
        their numbers come out in the left-to-right order in which the page
        shows them.
      - Three things cannot be known from a page alone: (a) a Latin word next to
        a number could have been typed in either order (`5 GB` is drawn `GB 5`
        and comes out `GB 5`); (b) a number at the start of a line that
        continues a paragraph is read as if the line began there; (c) a file
        printed from Word through a virtual printer does not identify itself as
        Word in metadata, so slash-separated dates in it come out as the page
        shows them.
      - Runs of spaces are collapsed to a single space (runs of three or more
        spaces are **not** converted into tabs, because font width quirks
        frequently produce wide space runs inside ordinary phrases). Table
        columns in PDFs are not marked; cells of a row are separated by one
        space, rightmost cell first on a right-to-left page.
    - Password-protected files that do not open with an empty password fail with
      `validation`; an unreadable page yields an empty page and a note; without
      `pypdf` installed, reading PDF text returns `validation` with a hint
      naming `ews-mcp[extract]`.
  - **Word (`.docx`, `.docm`, `extracted_from: "docx"`)** via stdlib `zipfile`
    + `defusedxml`: paragraphs in document order and tables as one line per row
    with tab-separated cells, reading only `mc:Choice` inside
    `mc:AlternateContent` so text boxes are not duplicated. Macros are never
    read.
  - **Excel (`.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `extracted_from: "xlsx"`, `sheets`,
    `sheets_read`)**: each worksheet is streamed under `--- Sheet: <name> ---`
    with tab-separated cell values (shared strings, inline strings, booleans,
    numbers, and cached formula values), stopping at `5,000` rows and `50`
    columns per sheet (so worksheets larger than the `20` MiB single-XML-part
    limit still return their first `5,000` rows with a cut note and `partial:
    true` instead of an error) and `2,000` characters per cell; number formats
    from `xl/styles.xml` render dates and times in ISO form (`YYYY-MM-DD`,
    `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:SS]`, `HH:MM[:SS]`, supporting both `1900` and `1904`
    workbook date systems) and percentages as percentages (if `xl/styles.xml`
    cannot be read, raw numbers are returned with a note); cell references
    longer than `10` characters fail with `validation`.
  - **PowerPoint (`.pptx`, `.pptm`, `extracted_from: "pptx"`, `slides`,
    `slides_read`)**: slides in presentation order under `--- Slide N ---`
    (including slide tables).
  - **Mail and HTML**: RFC-822 `.eml` (`extracted_from: "eml"`, parsed under
    `compat32` with raw 8-bit header bytes recovered as UTF-8 falling back to
    `Windows-1256` before the `4,000`-character header cut, and at most `50`
    addresses listed per header) and attached Exchange items
    (`extracted_from: "message"`) return main headers, plain or cleaned HTML
    body, and nested attachment names; `.html`/`.htm` (`extracted_from:
    "html"`) and every document/HTML body in `get_attachment` run through the
    isolated child worker; `.txt`/`.csv`/`.md`/`.log`/`.json` and plain-text
    MIME attachments (`extracted_from: "text"`) decode and slice directly in the
    server process without spawning a worker (decoding only as many UTF-8 or
    BOM-marked UTF-16 bytes as `5,000,000` characters can need, with no per-line
    processing or line-ending normalisation, and lone surrogates replaced with
    `U+FFFD`). Text-like files are never refused for their leading bytes. S/MIME
    attachments (`.p7m`, `.p7s`) keep their binary / `smime_type` handling
    across every mode. Outlook `.msg` message files are not decoded as text: in
    both `mode="auto"` and `mode="text"` they return `mode: "info"` with a
    `note` and `hint` instructing the caller to save them (`mode='save'`) and
    open them externally.
- **Unsupported binaries.** In `mode="auto"`, unsupported binary attachments
  return `mode: "info"` with a `mode='save'` hint without downloading bytes,
  and `mode="auto"` always returns the same result whether or not an earlier
  call cached the attachment. In `mode="text"`, other unsupported binary types
  return `validation` with `hint` listing the supported formats.
- **Reading in parts, `partial`, `notes`, and memory cache.** Assembled text
  stops at `5,000,000` characters. Pass `offset` (characters, default `0`) to
  page through long documents in `20,000`-character slices. Every extracted-text
  result carries `offset`, `total_chars`, `extracted_from`, `next_offset` (when
  more text follows), `partial: true` whenever the extracted text is not the
  whole document (time limit, character limit, or row/column/sheet/page/slide/MIME
  limits), `notes` (a list of at most `8` notes of at most `300` characters
  each, with cut notes placed first and never dropped, and repeated notes of the
  same kind folded into one with a count; `note` also joins them for single-string
  consumers), and the unit counts (`pages`/`pages_read`, `slides`/`slides_read`,
  or `sheets`/`sheets_read`). Every paged part repeats `partial` and `notes`.
  Extracted text is cached in memory only: at most `4` documents and `8,000,000`
  characters in total, with a `10`-minute TTL, keyed by `(attachment_id, size)`
  (or an unambiguous tuple of message id, attachment index, name, and size when
  Exchange provides no attachment id). Later parts (`offset > 0`) are served
  from memory only through the exact `(message_id, attachment)` selector seen on
  an earlier call (starting no worker and making no Exchange calls); if an
  unseen selector is passed with `offset > 0`, the picker resolves it with a
  single metadata fetch and serves the cached entry without re-downloading or
  re-extracting.
- **Hostile-input bounds.** Attachments above `EWS_MAX_ATTACHMENT_MB` (by declared size
  before download and by the bytes that arrive; `mode="save"` parses nothing and
  writes what Exchange delivers), ZIP
  members using compression methods other than stored or deflated, archives
  with more than `2,000` members (checked before reading any member), non-streamed
  members exceeding `30` MiB read or XML parts exceeding `20` MiB, archives
  exceeding `100` MiB read in total, XML trees deeper than `256` elements,
  DTD/entity XML constructs, and truncated or mislabelled document files all
  fail closed with `validation` errors of at most `300` characters (echoing at
  most `80` characters of file-supplied text) without tripping the server
  circuit breaker.

## Inbox rules

Three tools manage Exchange's server-side Inbox rules (`list_rules` at
`read`, stamped `source: "live"`; `save_rule` and `delete_rule` at `draft`,
both class `write` on purpose so a `draft`-tier caller can undo its own rule,
with audit records keeping the dispatcher's standard format, and both always
two-phase confirmed):

- **Safety contract (mailbox-internal only, fail-closed folder verification).**
  `save_rule` builds `Actions` strictly from six allow-listed fields:
  `move_to_folder`, `copy_to_folder`, `assign_categories`, `mark_as_read`,
  `mark_importance`, and `stop_processing_rules`. Actions that send, forward,
  redirect, auto-reply, send SMS alerts, or delete mail are never writable.
  `move_to_folder` and `copy_to_folder` refuse Deleted Items, Junk Email, and
  any folder below them (matched by `DeletedItems` / `JunkEmail` class,
  `DISTINGUISHED_FOLDER_ID`, `WELL_KNOWN` name, or raw id), fail closed if the
  Deleted Items or Junk Email ids cannot be determined (unless Exchange reports
  `ErrorFolderNotFound`), verify the target folder's live `parent_folder_id`
  ancestry up to `msg_folder_root` (bounded to 25 levels) in both phases, and
  always send a real `FolderId`.
- **Read-only reporting for complex or unreadable rules.** `list_rules` returns
  every rule with an `r`-alias id (never minting `r` aliases for nonexistent
  rule ids, and resolving each distinct target folder at most once per call).
  Any rule that uses a non-writable action, an exception, a condition outside
  the writable set (`from_addresses`, `sent_to_addresses`, `subject_contains`,
  `body_contains`, `subject_or_body_contains`, `sender_contains`,
  `recipient_contains`, `has_attachments`, `importance`, `sent_to_me`,
  `sent_cc_me`, `sent_only_to_me`, `sent_to_or_cc_me`, `not_sent_to_me`), a
  present-but-unreadable XML element, a move/copy target without a readable
  folder id or resolvable label, or `is_not_supported` is reported with
  `editable: false` and the field names in `unsupported` (plus `sends_mail:
  true` and `recipients` when it sends or forwards mail, and `in_error: true`
  when Exchange flags a broken rule). `save_rule` refuses to replace any rule
  with `editable: false` so unsupported fields are never silently dropped. On a
  replace (`rule_id` provided), omitting `priority` or `enabled` preserves the
  current rule's value, and the phase-1 preview includes `changes` (the list of
  top-level rule field names that differ between `current` and `rule`).
- **Token binding, serialisation, write verification, and disabled-rule
  deletion.** `save_rule` and `delete_rule` are serialised in-process under one
  lock. Their confirmation token binds the planned rule (including raw target
  folder ids), the rule being replaced or deleted (including a SHA-256
  fingerprint of its serialised XML), and the `outlook_only_rules` flag;
  unrelated rules changing in between do not invalidate the token. Rule writes
  call `CreateInboxRule`, `SetInboxRule`, and `DeleteInboxRule` directly and
  treat read-back as a separate step: if the write succeeded on Exchange and
  read-back failed, `save_rule` returns `ok: true` with `verified: false`, the
  planned rule (`id: null` on create), and a `note` instructing the caller to
  run `list_rules`. When `delete_rule` targets a disabled rule and Exchange
  answers `ErrorItemNotFound`, it neutralises the rule into an enabled no-match
  rule (a fresh 48-character random `contains_subject_strings` token and
  `stop_processing_rules` only) before deleting it.
- **Outlook rule-blob caveat.** Modifying or deleting rules via EWS
  `UpdateInboxRules` sends `RemoveOutlookRuleBlob=true`, which deletes
  client-side send rules and can cause rules disabled via the Outlook UI to be
  lost. `list_rules` reads `OutlookRuleBlobExists` from Exchange and reports
  top-level `outlook_only_rules` (`true|false|null`). Both `save_rule` and
  `delete_rule` surface an explicit warning in their phase-1 preview whenever
  `outlook_only_rules` is `true` or `null` (and `save_rule` also warns when a
  rule has no conditions and therefore matches every incoming message).

## Intentionally dropped vs v3

Removed deliberately — most belong to the calling assistant (skills), not
a data-plane server:

- **One-shot send tools** (`send_email`, `reply_email`, `forward_email`):
  the ONLY way mail leaves the mailbox is `create_draft` → `send_draft`.
- **Impersonation / delegated mailboxes** (`target_mailbox` everywhere):
  one server = one mailbox.
- **OAuth2/MSAL flows**: the target deployment is on-prem Exchange with
  auto-negotiated auth; a Graph/OAuth backend would be a different
  gateway, not a flag.
- **Contacts folder management** (create/update/delete contacts).
- **Folder management** (create/rename/delete folders).
- **Raw MIME content in tool responses** (`get_message(format="eml")`
  saves the `.eml` file exclusively under `DATA_DIR/attachments` —
  adding `-2`, `-3`, … rather than overwriting, capping the filename stem
  at 200 UTF-8 bytes, and returning `internal` without tripping the
  Exchange circuit breaker if the attachment folder cannot be written —
  and returns only `saved_path` and `size_bytes`; note that a message
  exported from Sent Items may contain its `Bcc` header because the file
  is the message as the mailbox holds it).
- **The agent-secretary stack** (server-side classify/summarize/brief/
  voice/commitments/approval queue): the caller already IS an LLM;
  `examples/skills/exchange-assistant/` shows the skill-side pattern.
